name: Alloderm lip augmentation

lead: AlloDerm is donor skin from cadavers that has been processed to remove living cells. In lip augmentation, surgeons have placed it in small rolls in the lip or along the border of the lip to add size or sharpen the edge, according to Wikipedia.
A 2000 paper in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery is titled "Alloderm lip augmentation", but its abstract was not available, and no outcome data were found in the sources reviewed.

paras: Rolled or layered donor dermal tissue is inserted into the lip mucosa to add bulk, or into the vermilion border to define it.
The sources reviewed give no specific complication data for this use. Wikipedia lists general lip augmentation complications such as swelling, bruising, asymmetry and lumpiness.

trials.title: Vestibular Socket Therapy Using Acellular Dermal Matrix Versus Connective Tissue Graft

lead: AlloDerm lip augmentation uses processed donor (cadaver) dermis to add volume to the lips. Wikipedia says it is placed in small rolls in the mucosa to add size, or in the vermilion to sharpen the lip border [1].
A paper titled "Alloderm lip augmentation" appeared in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery in 2000 [2]. Beyond that, no outcome data were found in the sources reviewed.

paras: The material is human dermis processed to remove viable cells and used as a graft [1]. Wikipedia describes two placements in lip work: rolls inside the mucosa for volume and a strip at the vermilion to define the lip edge [1].

No studies found beyond a single 2000 journal paper whose abstract was not available [2]. A registered dental trial of acellular dermal matrix for tooth-socket therapy is unrelated to lip augmentation.

timeline.event: "Alloderm lip augmentation" is published in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery [2].
